newsitem.title: USA: Christmas lights, Oasis test boost U.S. West power.
newsitem.headline: Christmas lights, Oasis test boost U.S. West power.

text.p: Hanging of Christmas lights and test runs of new transmission pricing, as well as colder weather, helped boost spot power prices in the U.S. West, market sources said Wednesday.
The onset of holiday lighting typically adds 200 to 300 megawatts (MW) to loads within Southern California Edison Co's service territory alone, a company source said.

Spot power prices jumped sharply Wednesday, due in large part to a renewed rally in spot natural gas prices, but market sources noted that demand has gone up, possibly by a larger-than-anticipated amount.
"A lot of preschedulers probably planned last Wednesday for Monday needs, but the weather down here turned out to be colder than expected," said one southern California trader.
Traders also cited forecasts for a cold front moving into northern California and the Northwest as adding to this week's market tightness.
In addition, test runs began this week of the OASIS transmission pricing system mandated under the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's (FERC) order on open transmission access.
"People are unsure about what's going to happen - I think the uncertainty is keeping prices high," said a Southwest utility trader.
Another market source said tests began in phases starting Monday through Wednesday, meaning that some utilities had added transmission costs to their prices before others.
"People have to start acting as if they are charging themselves the same transmission costs they are charging everyone else," she said.
By the time the system is fully in place - January 3 under the FERC mandate - utilities and marketers will have the same transmission costs, but sources anticipate some bumps. The
Bonneville Power Administration began adding transmission costs to its surplus power offers on October 1, resulting in an immediate price jump of $1.00-2.00 per megawatt hour.
